advancedSettingsHint.message: Override token estimation coefficients per platform. Changes require refreshing the AI platform page.

coeffDescription.message: Estimate tokens per character (CJK/Kana/Hangul) or per word (Cyrillic/Arabic/Latin). Higher = more tokens for that script.

estimationGuideText.message: Headroom estimates token counts from the conversation text using per-script coefficients — it never trusts the platform's own count. CJK ideographs, Japanese kana, and Korean Hangul are counted per character. Cyrillic, Arabic, and Latin (and anything else) are counted per whitespace-separated word. Each script has a coefficient that represents the average tokens per counting unit for that model's tokenizer, calibrated by observing real tokenizer output. You can adjust these coefficients per platform in the Advanced settings above.

platformRefNoteDeepseek.message: Measured against the open DeepSeek-V4 tokenizer (exact). Chinese is cheap: ~0.6 tok/ch; Cyrillic/Arabic ~2.1 tok/wd.

platformRefNoteChatgpt.message: Measured offline with tiktoken o200k_base (exact). CJK ~0.8 tok/ch; Latin ~1.3 tok/wd.

platformRefNoteGemini.message: Tokenizer not public; measured via Gemma, which Google states is the same tokenizer. CJK ~0.7 tok/ch.

platformRefNoteKimi.message: Measured against the open K2.6 tiktoken vocab (exact). Chinese ~0.6 tok/ch; Cyrillic/Arabic words are costly (~2.8 tok/wd).

platformRefNoteQwen.message: Measured against the open Qwen3.6 tokenizer — the closest open sibling of the web model. CJK ~0.6 tok/ch.

platformRefNoteQianwen.message: Same tokenizer family as Qwen — shares the same measured coefficients.

platformRefNoteDoubao.message: Closed tokenizer; measured via ByteDance's open Seed-OSS as proxy. Tune if the gauge drifts — kana is the least reliable value.

aboutStack.message: Built with WXT, Vitest, and TypeScript.
